question: A client asks a project lead to confirm in writing that material shared during the engagement will not be used to train Anthropic's models. What is the appropriate first step before he answers?
options: A) Confirm which Claude plan the engagement's work is actually being carried out on.
B) Tell the client the team will use incognito chats throughout the whole engagement.
C) Assure the client that no Anthropic product ever trains on any customer material.
D) Send the client the instructions for changing model improvement privacy settings.
correct_answers: A) Confirm which Claude plan the engagement's work is actually being carried out on.
explanations: Correct. The answer depends entirely on which plan the work sits on: commercial products such as Claude for Work do not use inputs and outputs for model training by default, whereas on personal Free, Pro and Max accounts it turns on a user-controlled setting. He cannot answer honestly until he knows which applies.

Incognito chats are never used to improve Claude, but reaching for that before knowing how the team actually works substitutes a workaround for an accurate answer, and would not suit an engagement's ongoing work.
This is too broad to be true. It ignores the difference between commercial and consumer plans, and would be an inaccurate written assurance if any of the work is happening on personal accounts.
Those instructions cover personal accounts only. Sending them implies the engagement runs on consumer plans, which he has not established and which may misrepresent the arrangement.
